name: Tom hum do
summary: A small red lobster nicknamed fire lobster, with firmer, sweeter meat than other lobsters. Vietnam Tourism calls Côn Đảo a lobster-farming kingdom, yet also says this lobster cannot be farmed and is caught only in the wild.
origin: Côn Đảo. Vietnam Tourism, and Báo Điện Biên Phủ, 31 July 2026.
taste: Firmer and sweeter meat than other lobsters.
howToEat: Eat it steamed whole, in soup, in salad, or as sushi. In winter a female may carry golden roe along the spine.
where: Seaside restaurants in town. Báo Điện Biên Phủ lists tôm hùm on their menus.
seoTitle: Tom hum do — red lobster in Con Dao
seoDescription: Tôm hùm đỏ, the Côn Đảo fire lobster, is smaller than other lobsters with firmer, sweeter meat, steamed whole or served as sushi.
